references.text: Gideon makes the same request to the men of Penuel, who also refuse to help him
Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian whom Gideon pursues, are finally captured
The context for the pursuit of the Midianites that led to Gideon's arrival at Sukkot
Sukkot is mentioned as a place where Jacob built shelters and gave the place its name
A similar situation where the Israelites were exhausted and needed help during their journey
David sends men to ask for food in a situation similar to Gideon's
David's men were too exhausted to continue the pursuit, like Gideon's men
Zebah and Zalmunna are mentioned as examples of God's victory over Israel's enemies
